subject: thm-cyclotomic-schur-standards-and-schur-functor-control-block-linkage
inspection_scope: Only F3 nonzero-cell qualification and existing seven flagged case contexts; no new whole mathematical audit
F3_before:
[F3] For a finite-dimensional cellular algebra over a field with cell modules
$C_\lambda$ and quotients $D_\lambda=C_\lambda/R_\lambda$: every nonzero
$D_\lambda$ is an absolutely simple head, all simple modules occur exactly
once, $[C_\lambda:D_\mu]\ne0\Rightarrow\lambda\ge\mu$ and
$[C_\mu:D_\mu]=1$; every nonzero cell module has all composition factors in
one block, and two cell modules share a block exactly when linked by a finite
chain of cell modules with neighbouring terms sharing a simple factor
([[lem-finite-cellular-nonzero-form-heads-purity-and-shared-factor-linkage]]).
F3_after:
[F3] For a finite-dimensional cellular algebra over a field with cell modules
$C_\lambda$ and quotients $D_\lambda=C_\lambda/R_\lambda$: every nonzero
$D_\lambda$ is an absolutely simple head, all simple modules occur exactly
once, $[C_\lambda:D_\mu]\ne0\Rightarrow\lambda\ge\mu$ and
$[C_\mu:D_\mu]=1$; every nonzero cell module has all composition factors in
one block, and two nonzero cell modules share a block exactly when linked by a
finite chain of nonzero cell modules with neighbouring terms sharing a simple factor
([[lem-finite-cellular-nonzero-form-heads-purity-and-shared-factor-linkage]]).

cases.existing_case_explanation: For a single-box multipartition the canonical semistandard tableau still gives an idempotent projection with unit self-pairing; the head and weight calculations therefore include it without a positive-rank exception.
cases.actual_clause_use_assessment: The canonical tableau has unit self-pairing in unchanged proof1.2 and weight calculation1.4, so its Schur standard is nonzero before any purity premise is applied.

cases.existing_case_explanation: All multipartition cell layers and tableau bases are finite, and each heredity layer is removed by its specified unit Gram entry; finite composition-series and exact-corner arguments introduce no arbitrary-family choice.
cases.actual_clause_use_assessment: The finite tableau bases, unit Gram heredity construction and exact corner argument are unchanged; excluding zero general cell modules introduces no selection or Choice use.

cases.existing_case_explanation: The block comparison has no analytic endpoint: the finite dominance chain explicitly removes each maximal remaining cell layer until completion, and the center maps are algebraic at every layer.
cases.actual_clause_use_assessment: The finite heredity-layer argument remains unchanged and all Schur standards possess the distinguished tableau; the analytic-endpoint exclusion does not rely on an unqualified zero-cell linkage claim.

cases.existing_case_explanation: Coincident charges or a nonsemisimple Hecke specialization do not remove the canonical unit self-pairing of a Schur standard; its head remains nonzero, while the exact corner is expressly allowed to send that head to zero.
cases.actual_clause_use_assessment: A Schur standard still has the canonical unit Gram entry, including singular Hecke parameters; its potentially zero simple corner is not a zero cell module. The corrected F3 clause leaves this distinction intact.

cases.existing_case_explanation: The corner image of a Schur simple is allowed to be zero, and composition multiplicities are transferred only for nonzero Specht heads; the radical equality proves this allowance rather than presuming a bijection of all simple labels.
cases.actual_clause_use_assessment: The existing explanation concerns a possibly zero image of a Schur simple, not a zero Specht cell module. Proof2.2 retains the radical/corner equality and transfers multiplicities only when the Specht head is nonzero.

cases.existing_case_explanation: A Schur-standard block idempotent corresponds under the center isomorphism to the Hecke block idempotent acting on its nonzero Specht corner, so two standards in the same Schur block have Spechts in the same Hecke block.
cases.actual_clause_use_assessment: Proof1.2 establishes nonzero Schur standards and proof3.1 establishes nonzero Specht corners from their standard-tableau bases, so corrected nonzero-cell block purity/linkage applies to the forward block-idempotent comparison.

cases.existing_case_explanation: The inverse center map lifts the Hecke block idempotent to its action on the permutation-module sum; nonzero Specht corners determine the corresponding block-pure Schur standards, giving the reverse block-linkage direction.
cases.actual_clause_use_assessment: The same nonzero Schur standards and Specht corners allow the inverse center-idempotent comparison. A zero intermediate cell cannot share a simple factor with a neighbor and therefore cannot create an edge in the chain already used in unchanged proof3.1.
